title: Wait on pthread_cond_wait in a while loop
summary: Move the consumer wait from if to while, then make push wait when the queue is full.

turns.user: went to 4 consumer threads and sometimes one reads from an empty queue. fine with 1 thread

assistant.body: TL;DR: pthread_cond_broadcast wakes every waiting consumer for a single item, so the second one onward reads an empty queue. Switching to pthread_cond_signal wakes exactly one.

turns.user: switched to signal, still happens. less often

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. POSIX allows pthread_cond_wait to return with no signal at all, the so called spurious wakeup. On top of that, another consumer can take the item before the woken thread gets the mutex back. The condition has to be rechecked in a while loop every time the thread wakes. Keeping signal is fine.

turns.user: also push overwrites when it's full right? make that wait too

assistant.body: Good catch. When count is 16 it still writes, stomping on the oldest item. Adding a second condition variable, not_full, which pop signals after taking an item. push waits on it in a while loop for the same reason. Note: sharing one condition variable between producers and consumers lets a signal land on the wrong side, and everyone can end up waiting. Remember to pthread_cond_init the new one wherever the queue is set up.

turns.user: 16 is too small, things back up. 64

assistant.body: Every 16 in this file means capacity, so a global replace is safe. Pulling it into a constant would be more robust, but this keeps the diff minimal.
